additional_provenance_gap.fix: Capture one initial revision/tree, compare blobs against that fixed revision, require final HEAD/tree equal it, and validate runner/worker buildinfo revision and clean status. Test-binary provenance should be bound through the frozen source inventory; do not invent VCS fields absent from Go test build info.
additional_provenance_gap.reason: snapshot compares each file with the current mutable HEAD; initial/final clean status plus equal non-evidence bytes do not prove the same revision was used throughout. A commit affecting only excluded evidence, or an identical-tree commit, can move HEAD during the three builds. Build-info output is retained but never checked for the expected vcs.revision/vcs.modified=false.
additional_provenance_gap.severity: P2 evidence identity if HEAD changes concurrently

p1_p2_findings.fix: Reuse the reviewed prepare.read_preparation for fixed identity/helper binding; validate all existing output-parent directory chains with no symlinks and intended ownership/mode, especially BASE/bin and OUT/ARCHIVE parents; use lexists for runtime/acceptance/partial outputs. Retain all failures.
p1_p2_findings.reason: A symlinked BASE/bin passes current existence checks and directs the first Go output outside the fresh scope. Dangling runtime/acceptance entries are ignored by exists(). preparation.json is only is_file(), not a validated descriptor. The recording fixtures intercept before any build process; the exact unsafe output argument is retained.
p1_p2_findings.title: Scope preflight follows path substitutions and misses partial dangling entries

p1_p2_findings.basis: Read-only confirmation from installed Python subprocess.run source plus recorded invocation keywords; no runaway process experiment was executed.
p1_p2_findings.fix: Reuse the previously reviewed execute_bounded process-group wrapper, or create a new session per command and always bounded TERM→KILL/wait only that command group on failure/timeout. Keep failed command/source/partial-binary evidence.
p1_p2_findings.reason: The actual source calls subprocess.run(timeout=300) without an isolated process group. Local Python subprocess.run TimeoutExpired kills/waits only the direct go process, so spawned compiler/linker processes can survive and continue writes after the build controller reports failure.
p1_p2_findings.title: Build timeout does not terminate compilation descendants

safe_properties: Only three fixed binary output names and two exact test enumeration names are used; no acceptance test invocation or provider/socket action is present.
Go module/proxy/toolchain network settings are explicitly disabled, log/output filenames are exclusive, prior attempt outputs are retained, and archival happens after verification.
The ordinary UID1000/clean-checkout guards and executable hashing are useful but do not close the directory-chain or process-descendant gaps.
scope: independent source review and isolated temporary-path/recording mocks only; no Go build/test, Git mutation, PG, Docker, systemd, mount or service action
